change: the Command Center retry panel controls the policy the server enforces, instead of moving the numbers on the page and saving nothing
_reported: Tanner, 2026-09-09: "I also have students able to retry assignments as many times as they want." The engine was fine. The panel was four per-type switches tagged SAVING SOON that wrote to page state and called renderAll, so a teacher turning Quizzes off watched the grades move and changed nothing a student could do. Worse than an inert control: moving numbers is exactly the feedback a working one gives.
_why_three_and_not_four: classes.retry_mode holds all / practice / none. Four per-type switches is 16 combinations of which the server can hold three, so wiring four toggles to three modes would refuse the teacher 13 times out of 16. The panel is a three-way choice now and every state it can reach is one the server has. Labels and blurbs are retry-policy.js's own MODE_LABELS and MODE_DESCRIPTIONS, copied verbatim so the two surfaces cannot describe the same rule differently.
_the_ride_along: This sheet also carries work that is already in shopify/cyber-dashboard.html and was never imported: board 260's unenforceable-lock disclosure, which adds a warning glyph beside the padlock and moves the reason into aria-label. Measured against the live body 2026-09-09: the glyph is absent live and present in the repo. That is finished, reviewed work from 2026-09-07 whose run note says in as many words that the sheet needed a human to import it, and stripping it back out by hand would be worse than shipping it. Flagged rather than folded in silently. The remaining four diff hunks are entity round-trip noise: the repo writes – and ▾ where the live body holds the decoded characters, and Shopify decodes them again on import.
_not_changed_here: The per-student retry rows on the By Student tab. They still do not save, and they still say so on the card: "Preview only in this session. These four do not save yet." Writing one is a single call; reading it back is not, because the teacher progress payload carries no retry_override field, so a wired toggle would show Default on the next load while an override was live. That is a payload change and its own piece of work.
